# Stage-1 kernels on H1: mappings, MFU factors and checks

<!-- generated by `python -m workload_modeling.kernel_explorer`; do not edit by hand -->

Companion to [smolvla-op-graph.md](smolvla-op-graph.md) and [smolvla-op-graph-w1b.md](smolvla-op-graph-w1b.md). For every kernel shape of the composed call it shows the mapping space the drivers in `infra/kernel-runs/` could choose from, what was swept, what was selected, and where the selected kernel loses MFU. The interactive version (mesh diagrams, candidate scatter, Perfetto links) is `infra/workload-modeling/build/kernel-explorer.html`; serve it with `python3 infra/kernel-runs/serve_traces.py`.

Labels: kernel times, sweep rows and trace events are *measured*; the valid space counts come from the drivers' candidate generators (*inference*); MFU factors, the time budget and busy fractions are *estimate*.

132 of 134 checks pass.

* **pick**: the selected setting (the one constants.yaml was made from) is the fastest run with a passing output check over every result set of the shape (`gemm_sweep_h1.csv`, `gemm_smallm_h1.csv`, `gemm_transpose_h1.csv`; row kernels: `row_kernels_h1.csv`, `eltwise_pipeline_h1.csv`).
* **constants**: the re-run time in `final_h1.csv` is the time in `constants.yaml` (`h1_kernels`).
* **placement**: for every traced setting, the clusters the kernel's group placement makes active (`placement()`, from `flex_group_barrier.h:43` and `SummaGEMM.h:131-138`) are exactly the clusters with RedMulE activity in the kernel window of the trace (`results/trace_summary_h1.json`). Coverage: the traces are of square groups (1x1, 2x2) and attention only. The selected non-square and splitK expert mappings and the scale-8 picks have no trace, so their mesh diagrams rest on the kernel source alone.
* **sum**: count x kernel time over all operators gives the composed time of the operator-graph page.

## Where the time goes (estimate)

Each matrix kernel's time split as: ideal (true FLOP at the 131.1 TFLOP/s peak) + padding (padded FLOP, same rate: shape padding to whole tiles, and for GEMM RedMulE array padding to whole 32 x 64 output blocks, see below) + idle clusters (padded FLOP on only the active clusters) + HBM floor (the extra time if the operator's unique bytes, each moved once, need longer at 1,024 GB/s than the compute above; that bandwidth is an inference, the memspec alone gives half, which would double this column) + rest (time beyond that roofline: tiling re-reads, NoC, synchronisation, per-call overhead, HBM below peak). Row operators (vector cores) are counted whole. MFU = ideal / total. Times in ms per call.

MFU here counts only matrix-kernel FLOP; the operator-graph page also counts the row operators' few FLOP, so it can differ in the last digit.

## Matrix kernels

MFU = f_pad x f_occ x f_rest. f_pad = true / padded FLOP = shape padding x RedMulE block fill (below); f_occ = active clusters / 64; f_rest = the rest, the matrix units' share of time inside the active clusters. Bound: which of the two lower limits, true FLOP at peak or the operator's unique bytes at 1,024 GB/s, is larger. Time in µs per call; total = over both pages' uses is not summed, see the operator-graph pages for call totals.

### f_pad in words

f_pad = shape padding x RedMulE block fill. Shape padding: the operator rounded up to whole tiles. Block fill: how much of the area RedMulE times holds the tile, since it times each call in whole 32 x 64 output blocks (a 128 x 96 tile runs as 128 x 128, block fill 0.75).

* `flatattention_12x1024x1024x64`: 1.00 = shape 1.00 (no padding) x block fill not modelled
* `flatattention_15x50x241x64`: 0.74 = shape 0.74 (q padded to 64, kv to 256) x block fill not modelled
* `flatattention_15x50x291x64`: 0.44 = shape 0.44 (q padded to 64, kv to 512) x block fill not modelled
* `flatattention_15x241x241x64`: 0.89 = shape 0.89 (q padded to 256, kv to 256) x block fill not modelled
* `gemm_50x32x720`: 0.27 = shape 0.55 (50x32x720 padded to 64x32x1024) x block fill 0.50 (tile 32x32 runs as 32x64)
* `gemm_50x720x32`: 0.55 = shape 0.55 (50x720x32 padded to 64x1024x32) x block fill 1.00 (tile fills whole blocks)
* `gemm_50x720x720`: 0.69 = shape 0.69 (50x720x720 padded to 64x768x768) x block fill 1.00 (tile fills whole blocks)
* `gemm_50x720x960`: 0.69 = shape 0.69 (50x720x960 padded to 64x768x1024) x block fill 1.00 (tile fills whole blocks)

### Why RedMulE block fill counts in f_pad

GVSoC's RedMulE model times every call in output blocks of 32 rows x 64 columns (redmule_h x redmule_w * (redmule_pipe + 1) from constants.yaml arch.h1), at redmule_pipe + 1 = 2 cycles per reduction element per block, however many of the block's columns hold data (`light_redmule.cpp`, `init_redmule_meta_data` and `get_redmule_array_runtime`). On H1 a tile of 128 x 96 thus takes the time of 128 x 128: 75 % of the array time does real MACs (block fill 0.75). This is counted with shape padding in f_pad, not left in f_rest, because:

* it is the same kind of loss: array time spent on work that is not in the operator (empty block slots instead of zero rows), at the full peak rate;
* the mapping fixes it before the kernel runs: it follows from the tile shape and the arch alone, so it can be computed for every candidate, traced or not, and a different tile or mapping removes it;
* f_rest then keeps only the run-time losses (data movement, synchronisation, per-call overhead, pipeline fill), which need traces or a cost model to explain.

The per-call rule ceil(m/32) x ceil(n/64) x k x 2 cycles + about 160 cycles matched the RedMulE event durations of 9 traced stage-1 GEMM shapes (estimate from a fit, 2026-11-23). Array padding is modelled for GEMM only: FlatAttention's RedMulE call shapes have not been read yet, so attention keeps block fill = 1. The interpretation that each CE interleaves ce_pipe + 1 outputs to hide the FMA latency is an inference; the timing rule itself is the simulator's code.

## Changes since stage 1

constants.yaml (h1_kernels) holds the W1 preset: per kernel the fastest checked run over every result set. Besides the stage-1 sweeps these are:

* **transposed GEMM** (20 runs; `infra/kernel-runs/gemm_transpose.py`, `results/gemm_transpose_h1.csv`), listed among each shape's candidates as `T:<setting>`: Z^T = W^T X^T, run as the GEMM N x M x K with gemm_sweep's candidates and output check. W^T is free (weights are laid out offline); X^T and Z^T are activation layouts the neighbouring operators would have to produce and accept, a cost not counted here.
* **pipelined Eltwise** (`infra/kernel-runs/eltwise_pipeline.py`, `results/eltwise_pipeline_h1.csv`; config `pipeline = 1`): the kernel stores row j-1 and loads row j+1 while Spatz computes row j (three row buffers); output identical (bad 0, max_ulp 0). Part of the gain comes from the code generated, not the overlap (the stage-1 loop compiled with the new struct alone was faster too); not separated.
